preamble: Secondary FSGS  |  Adaptive glomerular response to hyperfiltration from obesity, reduced nephron mass, sickle cell, reflux, or prior renal injury  |  Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost: Small = standard labs/exam  |  Medium = targeted workup ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = renal biopsy ($3,000–$10,000+)  |  KEY DISTINCTION: sub-nephrotic proteinuria, perihilar variant on biopsy, focal foot process effacement on EM — immunosuppression NOT indicated.

questions.question: Is proteinuria in the sub-nephrotic range (urine PCR 0.5–3.0 mg/mg or 24-hr protein 1–3.5 g/day)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — sub-nephrotic proteinuria confirmed; typical of secondary FSGS from hyperfiltration rather than primary podocyte injury

questions.question: Is serum albumin normal or only mildly reduced (≥3.0 g/dL) despite significant proteinuria?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — preserved albumin with sub-nephrotic proteinuria; distinguishes secondary FSGS from primary nephrotic syndrome

questions.question: Is onset insidious, discovered incidentally on routine urinalysis or labs rather than symptomatic nephrotic presentation?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — gradual asymptomatic onset consistent with adaptive hyperfiltration injury rather than acute podocyte collapse

questions.question: Is there morbid obesity (BMI ≥35) or significant weight gain temporally associated with onset of proteinuria?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — obesity-related FSGS confirmed as primary driver; most common cause of secondary FSGS worldwide

questions.question: Is there a documented history of solitary kidney, nephrectomy, prior renal transplant with reduced mass, renal dysplasia, or oligomeganephronia?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — reduced nephron mass confirmed; compensatory hyperfiltration in remaining nephrons drives adaptive FSGS

questions.question: Is there sickle cell disease (HbSS, HbSC) or sickle trait with documented sickle cell nephropathy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — sickle cell nephropathy confirmed; medullary infarction + hyperfiltration drive glomerular injury and FSGS

questions.question: Is there a history of vesicoureteral reflux (VUR Grade 3–5) or reflux nephropathy with renal scarring on imaging?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — reflux nephropathy confirmed; focal renal scarring reduces functional nephron mass causing hyperfiltration FSGS

questions.question: Is focal segmental glomerulosclerosis confirmed on light microscopy (segmental sclerosis <50% of glomeruli)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — FSGS pattern on LM confirmed; histologic diagnosis established

questions.question: Is the FSGS variant perihilar (sclerosis at the hilum with hyalinosis) on light microscopy? (perihilar is the hallmark of secondary/adaptive FSGS)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — perihilar variant confirmed; PATHOGNOMONIC for adaptive hyperfiltration FSGS; strongly supports secondary etiology

questions.question: Is foot process effacement focal and partial (<50% of glomerular capillary surface) on electron microscopy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — focal/partial foot process effacement confirmed; distinguishes secondary FSGS (focal) from primary FSGS (diffuse >80%); key EM differentiator

questions.question: Is there glomerulomegaly (enlarged glomerular tuft area >2 standard deviations above normal for age) on light microscopy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — glomerulomegaly confirmed; reflects compensatory hypertrophy from reduced nephron mass; supports adaptive FSGS diagnosis

questions.question: Does renal ultrasound or CT show asymmetric kidney size, cortical thinning, or scarring consistent with reduced nephron mass?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — structural renal abnormality confirmed on imaging; supports reduced nephron mass as driver of adaptive FSGS

questions.question: Are serum C3 and C4 complement levels normal and autoimmune serology (ANA, ANCA, anti-GBM) negative?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — immune-mediated GN excluded; supports non-immune adaptive etiology

questions.question: Is serum albumin ≥3.0 g/dL despite documented proteinuria (preserved synthetic function consistent with sub-nephrotic state)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — preserved albumin with sub-nephrotic proteinuria; reinforces secondary rather than primary FSGS pattern

questions.question: Is there no pathogenic podocyte gene variant identified on genetic testing (NPHS1, NPHS2, WT1, TRPC6, CD2AP, INF2, ACTN4)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — genetic primary FSGS excluded; podocyte gene panel negative

high.label: 🔴  80–100 High confidence
high.action: Secondary adaptive FSGS confirmed; TREAT THE CAUSE not the kidney: weight loss program for obesity-FSGS (target BMI <30; bariatric surgery if BMI >40); ACE inhibitor or ARB mandatory (proteinuria reduction and glomerular pressure lowering); SGLT-2 inhibitor for additive renoprotection; DO NOT initiate corticosteroids or immunosuppression — harmful in secondary FSGS

moderate.label: 🟡  50–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: Probable secondary FSGS; renal biopsy required to confirm perihilar variant and focal foot process effacement; identify and treat underlying cause before initiating any therapy; measure proteinuria response to RAS blockade over 3 months

low.label: 🟢  <50 Low confidence
low.action: Secondary FSGS insufficiently supported; consider primary FSGS (diffuse FPE, nephrotic presentation, tip/cellular variant) or other glomerular diseases; ensure all secondary causes have been systematically evaluated before pursuing immunosuppression
